record.original_question: For a ring R, we say that a group G is of type FL(R) if the trivial RG-module R admits a finite resolution by finitely generated free modules. If R is a field, we define the Euler characteristic of G over R to be the alternating sum of R-ranks of homology groups Hi(G; R). Does there exist a group of type FL(Fi) for two fields F1 and F2 such that the Euler characteristics of the group over the fields F1 and F2 differ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R be a (unital) ring and let G be a group. Say that G is of type FL(R) if the trivial RG-module R admits a finite resolution by finitely generated free RG-modules. When R is a field and G is of type FL(R), the homology groups H_i(G; R) are finite-dimensional R-vector spaces and vanish for all sufficiently large i; define the Euler characteristic of G over R by

  χ_R(G) = Σ_{i ≥ 0} (−1)^i dim_R H_i(G; R).

Question: Do there exist two fields F_1 and F_2 and a single group G that is simultaneously of type FL(F_1) and of type FL(F_2) such that χ_{F_1}(G) ≠ χ_{F_2}(G)?
